title: 50 members of European Parliament targeted by deepfake porn, report says
source_used: UA.NEWS relay of the Politico Europe report (the Politico page returned HTTP 403)
key_facts: A study by the German civil-society organisation Agora Digitale Transformation, reported by Politico Europe, found that 50 members of the European Parliament, including 46 women, have become targets of deepfake pornography.
The authors say the 46 women are about one-sixth of all women in the European Parliament.
Deepfake pornography means sexualised images of people created with generative AI, often without their consent.
From 2 December the EU introduces a ban on AI applications that can create nude images of people; the EU is also investigating similar tools linked to Grok on the X platform.

On 30 September an interparty group of 119 MEPs wrote to the Commission, Council and Parliament presidents and two commissioners, calling for effective enforcement of the ban and prompt completion of the Grok investigation.
Austrian Green MEP Lena Schilling, who signed the letter, said there can be no loopholes or delays in enforcing the ban.
Report co-author Benjamin Schulz said politicians find it hard to avoid such attacks because they cannot opt out of having their images online.

The authors say the Commission should hold accountable all parties that facilitate the industry, including payment operators and domain registrars, and propose considering removal of such sites from search indexes.
quote_evidence: In the European Union, 50 Members of the European Parliament, including 46 women, have become targets of deepfake pornography.
This is stated in a study by the German civil society organization Agora Digitale Transformation, Politico Europe reports.

On September 30, an interparty group of 119 MEPs sent a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, European Council President António Costa, European Parliament President Roberta Metsola, Henna Virkkunen, and European Commissioner Hadja Lahbib.
why_it_matters_hint: Deepfake pornography is already aimed at a sizeable share of the Parliament's women members, adding weight to calls to enforce the EU's coming ban.
event_date: Study reported 5 Oct 2026; MEPs' letter 30 Sep 2026; EU ban starts 2 Dec 2026
notes: Politico page blocked (HTTP 403); text read on the UA.NEWS relay, which summarises Politico Europe's report and names the study's authors. The study itself was not read. Politico link kept as the original. Brussels Signal and a Korean outlet (SBS) carried the same figures on 6 Oct.
